title: The Company of Wolves
review: It has the tone of a TV movie, although the production values are decent for the time. It was shot on film, and with lavish woodland sets, accompanied by a good score. It's just that there's a real 80s public television quality to the writing and acting. This is barely a horror and more of a spooky fairy tale anthology. It meanders between stories in a way I found a little hard to follow, but it's probably for the best because it stops that urge to compartmentalise the film into good and bad segments with real anthologies. It just didn't quite hold my attention as much as I'd hoped.
spoilers: It ends with a pretty good wolf transformation scene.
